evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: Creating a new game is a standalone feature and does not inherently require any other backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators by URL inherently requires a game (and its URL) to exist, which is created by PP-001.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round requires a game context to start the round in, which depends on PP-001 (create game).

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: To show all items for the session requires that items exist (be added), which is provided by PP-006 (add an item).

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item presumes items exist in the list, which requires PP-006 (add an item).

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding items is an action within a game session and thus requires a game to exist (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item presupposes the existence of items, which are created by PP-006 (add an item).

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item requires that items exist in the list, which depends on PP-006 (add an item).

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Showing estimates immediately presumes a round and estimates have been produced, which depends on starting a round (PP-003).

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average requires that multiple estimates exist for an item in a round, which requires PP-003 (start a round).

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Automatically filling the estimate depends on estimators showing cards in a round, which requires the round functionality from PP-003.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering an agreed estimate presumes a round and discussion have occurred (estimates exist), relying on PP-003 (start a round).

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating a previously estimated story requires that story to have been added/recorded earlier, created via PP-006 (add an item).

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories targets a game/session to import into, which presumes a game exists (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/pasting stories is intended to populate a game's item list and thus depends on having a game context (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games requires that prior games exist (created/stored by PP-001), so it depends on game creation/storage.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a game's transcript presumes the existence of stored game data (games created via PP-001), so it depends on game creation/storage.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript requires a transcript to exist (viewing/exporting transcripts is based on PP-017), so it depends on PP-017.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a CSV transcript similarly requires the transcript functionality, which is covered by PP-017.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game operates on an existing game resource, which must be created/stored first (PP-001).

evaluations.evidence: create an account for the application by entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Creating an account is a standalone operation and does not inherently require another backlog story first.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Logging in inherently requires an existing account, which is provided by PP-021 (create an account).

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details requires an existing account to change, which depends on PP-021 (create an account).

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an account presupposes the account exists, which is established by PP-021 (create an account).

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone display is a standalone presentation feature and does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminders require that an account and stored credentials exist, which depends on PP-021 (create an account).

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, ...} or {0, 1, 2, ...}
evaluations.rationale: Choosing the estimation scale is a configuration option and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators presumes an invitation mechanism and a game to invite to; it directly builds on PP-002 (invite estimators).

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining by URL requires that an invitation/URL has been generated for a game, which is provided by PP-002 (invite estimators).

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the current item requires a round to be started and an item to be presented, which depends on PP-003 (start a round).

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Providing participants a list of session items presumes the moderator-side listing functionality (PP-004), so it depends on PP-004.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Noticing individual estimates requires the ability to give estimates in a round, which depends on PP-003 (start a round/allow estimates).

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Displaying all estimates at once presumes the round/estimate collection mechanism (PP-003) is implemented.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: This change-until-show behavior depends on the simultaneous-show mechanic described in PP-033, so it depends on PP-033.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Showing prior estimates requires storage/access to previous estimates (history/transcript), which is provided by PP-039 (scroll back through prior rounds).

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Seeing per-estimator current-round estimates requires the round/estimate functionality (PP-003) that collects those estimates.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A shared countdown timer is a self-contained feature and does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Automatic reset on all estimates requires both the timer (PP-037) and the estimate-play detection; at minimum it depends on PP-037 for the timer.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling through prior rounds is a feature for navigating stored data; it does not inherently require a specific other backlog story to exist (it defines its own behavior).

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Card order consistency is a standalone UI/behavior requirement and does not inherently depend on another story.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Allowing estimate changes during a draw is a self-contained interaction rule and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a thumbnail near played cards is a presentational feature and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: have written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a cross-cutting development goal and is not inherently dependent on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Providing definitions is a standalone documentation task and does not inherently depend on other stories.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Creating database indexes is a developer task that does not inherently require another specific backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: have the application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser compatibility is an independent quality requirement and does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: have the site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is a standalone quality requirement and does not inherently require implementation of any other specific story first.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance responsiveness is a non-functional requirement and is self-contained, not inherently dependent on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a standalone capability and does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design is a self-contained requirement and does not inherently require another story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error page design is an independent feature and does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Anonymized storage is a privacy requirement and does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: be able to see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Collecting/seeing metrics is a self-contained feature request and does not inherently depend on another specific backlog story.
